headline: LinkedIn has spent $5,328 over 14 days with zero conversions and is paused; Meta is cut 20% as its CPA rose 1.7x; the direct surge tracks AI-assistant answers, not paid spend.

moves.reason: Zero conversions for 14 straight days (Oct 18-31) on $5,328 spend while daily spend rose from ~$300 to $460 (above the $450 budget). Prior 4-wk CPA was already $238 / ROAS 0.78. Self-reported LinkedIn share fell to 0% in the last 2 weeks, so this is probably not just a tracking break. Pause is cheap to reverse.

CPA rose from ~$60 to ~$100 (1.66x) since Oct 2 at flat spend (~$3.5k/wk); ROAS 3.2 to 1.9. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell from ~18% in Aug to 9% in the last week. A moderate 20% cut, not a pause, because attribution models disagree on Meta (CPA $45-$69) and a holdout test is better evidence.

tests.hypothesis: Meta's incremental CPA is below its reported $105 last-click CPA, because first-touch/Markov credit gives it 22%/20% against 14% last-touch. If so, the CPA rise since Oct 2 is partly a measurement problem and the 20% cut was too much.
tests.design: Geo holdout: switch Meta off in about 20% of matched regions for 4 weeks and keep it at $400/day elsewhere. Measure total conversions (tracked + direct) per region, plus self-reported 'Instagram or Facebook' share. Compare the drop in the held-out regions with the conversions Meta reports there. Pre-register a minimum detectable effect from the ~35 conversions per week baseline.

flag_verdicts.reason: Zero conversions Oct 18-31 on $5,328 while daily spend climbed from $300 to $460. Self-reported LinkedIn share is 0% for 2 weeks. Paused.
Meta CPA went from ~$60 to ~$100 at flat spend. Self-reported Instagram/Facebook share fell from ~18% to 9%. A real decline, so cut 20% and test rather than pause, since models disagree on Meta.
Sep 12-18 Google spend ran at 1.72x the median, but CPA moved only $18.33 to $20.56 (1.12x). Last 7 days CPA $18.77 vs $17.80 prior average. Efficiency held, so no action.

Direct rose from 1.5 to 8.1 conversions/day (5.4x) with paid spend at 1.05x. Self-reported 'AI assistant' plus 'Asked ChatGPT' rose from ~4% in Aug to ~28% last week. This points to AI-referral discovery. I credit no paid channel and move no budget; keep tracking.

flags.message: linkedin spent $5,328 over 14 days with zero conversions, and spend is still rising.
meta CPA rose 1.7x, from $60 to $100, starting 2026-10-02.
google_search spend jumped for 7 days (2026-09-12 to 2026-09-18); CPA held at $21 vs $18. Likely fine, confirm before acting.
Direct conversions grew 5.4x (1.5 to 8.1/day) while paid spend moved 1.05x. Self-reported AI answers went from 6% to 24%. Something untracked is driving buyers.
